skill.name: first-line-writer
skill.description: Drafts one outreach opener per prospect using public company or hiring facts collected through Leadsets. It records the supporting source and leaves the opener blank when no relevant fact is available.
skill.summary: Write prospect-specific outreach openers with source citations from company websites and careers pages.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: Of 26 static findings, only the operational Leadsets connection was confirmed; the other alerts matched formatting, reference links, or ordinary workflow text. No evidence found of shell execution, environment access, or a direct prompt injection attempt. The workflow lacks explicit safeguards for untrusted scraped content, paid scraping, and edits to connected destinations.

remediation.issue: Scraped content has no explicit instruction boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Treat scraped content as untrusted data, extract only factual fields, and prohibit that content from changing tool calls, destinations, or permissions.

remediation.issue: Paid scraping can begin without explicit spend approval.
remediation.suggestion: Request a unit cap before the paid probe, confirm the revised estimate before continuing, and stop at the approved cap.

remediation.issue: The workflow defaults to changing the source.
remediation.suggestion: Default to a separate draft and confirm the destination, rows, and fields before updating a connected sheet or campaign.

remediation.issue: The configured Leadsets service receives company domains.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the external processor before use and send only the company domains needed for scraping, not prospect names or email addresses.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Web Content Can Influence Drafts
semantic_findings.description: The workflow feeds public site and job content into drafting without telling the agent to ignore instructions embedded in the returned text. A page could influence generated text before it reaches the connected destination.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The steps connect scraped facts to draft generation and destination writes without an explicit trust boundary. No evidence found of an embedded instruction or an actual compromise.

semantic_findings.title: Paid Scraping Has No Explicit Approval Gate
semantic_findings.description: After checking the balance, the workflow calls a paid scraper for one domain and then instructs the agent to scrape the remaining domains. It requires showing a sample but does not require approval of the probe or remaining spend.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The steps distinguish available units from insufficient units but do not require a user-approved budget. The first sample comes after the paid probe.

semantic_findings.title: Default Writeback Modifies the Source
semantic_findings.description: The default is to add columns to the source, and the workflow allows updates to connected campaign fields. It does not require separate confirmation of the destination or affected records before writing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source default and connected write step are explicit. Actual modifications depend on the host connector's permissions and confirmation controls.

content.user_title: Write Outreach Openers With Company Facts
content.value_statement: Writing a distinct opening line for each prospect takes time, and generic lines do not show why the message is relevant. This skill drafts openers from public company facts and records the source so you can verify each line.
actual_capabilities: Groups prospects by company domain and reuses researched facts across prospects at the same company.
Checks available scrape units, tests the first domain, and reports units used.
Finds public facts on company websites and can use open roles with posting dates when hiring research is in scope.
Drafts one opener per eligible prospect and records the supporting fact, source, date, and status.
Exports a CSV or writes results to a connected destination.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets connection and paid scrape units. Free accounts cannot use the scraping tools.
Needs an existing prospect list and an offer description. It does not find, enrich, or verify contacts.
Does not read pages behind a login. It leaves lines blank when there is no relevant sourced fact or the input marks an email invalid.
Does not send or schedule outreach.

use_cases.title: Draft an Initial Outreach List
use_cases.description: Use public product facts to draft openers for a short list of prospective customers and check the source of each line.

use_cases.title: Find Relevant Hiring Signals
use_cases.description: Use dated job postings to open conversations with prospects whose companies are hiring for roles related to your offer.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client Campaign Drafts
use_cases.description: Create a separate CSV with sourced openers and reasons for blank rows before a client reviews the campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Draft One Opener
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Review a single homepage-based example.
prompt_templates.prompt: We sell inventory forecasting software. Write one opener for the first prospect in my CSV using the company homepage. Include the source and show the draft here.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Homepage-Based CSV
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: Research a list without editing the source.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these company homepages to draft one opener per prospect for our invoice approval software. Keep each line under 25 words and export a separate CSV. Leave rows blank when no relevant fact is available.

prompt_templates.title: Use Dated Hiring Signals
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Choose evidence based on its relevance to the prospect.
prompt_templates.prompt: We sell warehouse scheduling software. Prefer recent warehouse operations job postings when relevant, and otherwise use a company website fact. Return the source, fact date, and status for each row in a new CSV.

prompt_templates.title: Set a Budget and Review a Sample
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Control spend and review the draft before any destination update.
prompt_templates.prompt: We sell sales onboarding software. Estimate the scrape units for this campaign and ask before the first paid call. Show one sample and wait for approval before continuing. Export a separate CSV and do not update the campaign.

output_examples.input: Draft an opener for an operations lead. Our software forecasts inventory, and the example company homepage lists same-day dispatch.
output: Opening line: Your homepage lists same-day dispatch, and I wondered whether forecasting helps you keep stock available for those orders.
Supporting fact: The company offers same-day dispatch. Source: https://example.com/. Status: Written.

output_examples.input: Draft an opener for our warehouse scheduling offer using hiring signals only. The example company has no listed open roles.
output: Status: No hiring signal. The careers page listed no open roles.

best_practices: Provide first names, job titles, company domains, and a short description of what you sell.
Set a scrape unit budget and review one sample before approving the rest of the run.
Export a separate draft and check facts and sources before updating a shared sheet or campaign.
anti_patterns: Do not fill blank lines with generic praise or unsupported claims.
Do not treat a written line as proof that the prospect email address is verified.
Do not share unnecessary contact fields or update a campaign before checking the destination and affected rows.

faq.question: What columns does the input need?
faq.answer: Provide a first name, job title, and company domain for each prospect. Describe your offer separately.

faq.question: Can I choose which sources to use?
faq.answer: Yes. Request company websites, hiring signals, or both. When both are allowed, the skill prefers a relevant dated job posting.

faq.question: Can I run the scraper on a free Leadsets account?
faq.answer: No. Scraping requires a paid Leadsets plan with scrape units.

faq.question: Why did the skill leave some lines blank?
faq.answer: Rows can lack a relevant fact, have a failed scrape, or contain an email already marked invalid. The output records the reason.

faq.question: Where can I put the results?
faq.answer: Request a new CSV, a tab in the connected Google Sheet, or a custom field in a connected LinkedCamp, Instantly, or Smartlead campaign.

faq.question: Does this skill verify email addresses or send messages?
faq.answer: No. It preserves existing email statuses and only drafts opening lines. It does not send or schedule messages.
